column1: # Lines starting with '#' are comments and will be ignored by the parser.
# 1. Name                    - Unique identifier for the RNase
# 2. Motif                   - Cleavage motif syntax defining where cleavage occurs (see below)
# 3. Specificity             - One of: full, semi, none, SingleN, SingleC
# 4. CleavageModification    - Optional modification name from RnaMods.txt
# 5. CleavageModificationType - Optional fixed or variable behavior
# To add custom RNases (names that do not already exist in this file):
# 1. Create a TSV file with the same column format as this file
#   - If an RNase name matches an existing entry (embedded or already-loaded custom),
#     the custom entry is SKIPPED and the existing definition is retained
#   - If an RNase name is new, it will be ADDED to the dictionary
#   - The returned CustomDigestionAgentLoadResult lists which names were Added vs Skipped
# The motif syntax uses a simple pattern language:
#   |     = Cleavage point (where the phosphodiester bond is cut)
#   G[C]| = Cleave after G, UNLESS followed by C
#          (prevents cleavage when C is 3' to G)
# RNase T1:  G|           - Cleaves after G (guanosine-specific)
# RNase A:   "C|,U|"      - Cleaves after C or U (pyrimidine-specific)
# RNase T2:  "G|,C|,A|,U|" - Cleaves after any nucleotide
# full    - Both termini must match cleavage rules
# semi    - Only one terminus must match cleavage rules
# Given a sequence "ACGUGCA", single cleavage produces ladder fragments:
# Terminal modifications are represented as ordinary RNA modifications. The RNase definition
# references the modification by name and declares whether it is fixed or variable.
# Rnase.cs supplies the default internal termini; the modification is applied by digestion.
#   fixed    = apply the modification to every matching cleaved terminus
#   variable = generate modified and unmodified alternatives
